title: Anthropic’s IPO: Who Bears the Risk When the Compute Arrives?
homepageHeadline: Anthropic’s IPO puts the compute bill in public hands
dek: I traced Anthropic’s first public S-1 from its $80.7 billion loss to Note 8, conditional financing and founder control. The key question is what happens when committed compute meets flexible demand.

seo.title: Anthropic IPO S-1 Analysis: Profits, Compute Bills and Control
seo.description: A close reading of Anthropic’s October 26 S-1: the $80.7B loss, Note 8 margins, compute commitments, conditional financing and what ANT shareholders control.

faqs.question: Has Anthropic filed for an IPO?
faqs.answer: Yes. Anthropic, PBC publicly filed its initial Form S-1 on October 26, 2026, accession 0001628280-26-067168. The initial registration statement is not yet effective.

faqs.question: What is Anthropic’s proposed stock ticker and IPO price?
faqs.answer: The proposed ticker is ANT on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The October 26 S-1 leaves the IPO price range and number of offered shares blank, so it does not establish a final IPO valuation or trading date.

faqs.question: Did Anthropic burn $80.7 billion of cash in the first half of 2026?
faqs.answer: No. The $80.748 billion net loss includes large noncash financing revaluations. First-half operating cash flow was positive $3.929 billion, while the operating loss was $693 million. Future infrastructure funding needs are a separate question.

faqs.question: Will Anthropic’s public shareholders control the company?
faqs.answer: Class A stock has one vote per share, but the proposed Founder LLC Class F share carries 50.1% of general stockholder voting power. Separately, the Long-Term Benefit Trust generally elects directors constituting a board majority, subject to the governance provisions described in the filing.
